title: Transfer higher-direct-image vanishing from cyclic groups to constant module coefficients
statement:
Let $h:Y\to X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let $\Lambda$ be an arbitrary commutative ring, and let $d,q\in\mathbf N$. If $R^q h_*\underline{\mathbf Z/e}=0$ as an abelian sheaf for every $e\mid d$, then $R^q h_*\underline{\Lambda/d\Lambda}=0$ as a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules. Divisibility includes $0\mid0$ and $\mathbf Z/0=\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: Restrict the concrete quotient Lambda/(d) to lifted integers. The quotient equation makes d kill every element. Form its canonical diagram of finitely generated submodules, with the direct-limit cocone and Module.fgSystem.equiv. Each submodule has a finitely generated additive group. Apply the additive-functor cyclic vanishing lemma to coefficient forgetting followed by constant abelian sheafification and degree-q derived pushforward. The hypothesis H is exactly its cyclic hypothesis. No distinction between d=0 and d positive is needed here; the helper proves both.

Use coefficient-size filtered continuity of constant abelian higher direct images, and colimit preservation by forgetting integer scalars. Apply isColimitOfPreserves to the explicit direct-limit cocone. The image diagram consists of zero objects, so its colimit is zero. Map the canonical fgSystem linear equivalence and transport zero-ness to the underlying quotient.

The proved module/abelian higher-direct-image comparison for Lambda and the constant-sheaf coefficient comparison identify its forgotten higher image with the abelian higher image from the preceding step. The underlying sheaf functor preserves zero morphisms and is faithful; applying it to the identity detects zero-ness, giving the original module conclusion.
